title: Stable special function recurrences and certified evaluation

items.title: Airy initial-value series

references.title: N. M. Temme, “Numerical aspects of special functions,” Acta Numerica 17 (2008), §2

items.statement:
For $y(z)=\sum_{k\ge0}c_kz^k$, set $c_2=0$ and
$c_{k+3}=c_k/((k+3)(k+2))$ for $k\ge0$. Define $\operatorname{Ai}$ by this
series with

$$c_0=\frac{1}{3^{2/3}\Gamma(2/3)},\qquad c_1=-\frac{1}{3^{1/3}\Gamma(1/3)},$$

and define $\operatorname{Bi}$ by the same recurrence with

$$c_0=\frac{1}{3^{1/6}\Gamma(2/3)},\qquad c_1=\frac{3^{1/6}}{\Gamma(1/3)}.$$

Here $\Gamma$ is Euler's integral on the right half-plane from
[[def-euler-gamma-function]]. The standard Airy initial values are those in
DLMF §9.2(ii); in particular, the power of $3$ in $\operatorname{Bi}(0)$ is
in the denominator.

items.title: Certified special-function enclosure result

references.title: N. M. Temme, “Numerical aspects of special functions,” Acta Numerica 17 (2008), §§2–5

items.statement:
A **certified enclosure** for a real value is a nonempty closed interval
$B=[a,b]$ with finite dyadic endpoints; for a complex value it is a nonempty
closed rectangle $B=[a_1,b_1]+i[a_2,b_2]$ with finite dyadic endpoints. Its
radius is half its length in the real case and half its Euclidean diagonal in
the complex case; $d(B,0)$ is the Euclidean distance from $B$ to $0$.
An evaluator item declares whether its input is an exact dyadic point or a
dyadic interval/rectangle enclosure; a successful range result contains the
exact function image of every admissible point in an input enclosure. Constants
not exactly dyadic must be supplied with certified enclosing intervals or
rectangles.

The interval backend uses the endpoint operations in
[[def-outward-rounded-interval-and-ball-operations]]; the soundness of finite
arithmetic expression DAGs follows from
[[thm-outward-rounded-operations-are-isotone-and-dag-sound]]. Real elementary
function ranges use [[thm-real-elementary-range-enclosures]], and complex
exponential and principal-logarithm ranges use
[[thm-complex-elementary-range-enclosures]]. An operation that returns a
non-finite status supplies no finite enclosure claim.

A finite-budget evaluator receives a branch input enclosure wholly within
the stated domain, absolute tolerance $\varepsilon_a>0$, optional relative
tolerance $\varepsilon_r>0$, finite integer work and precision caps, and the
fixed format and truncation parameters required by the backend. Its result has
one of four statuses:

- `success`: the returned enclosure contains the exact requested value and its
  radius is at most $\varepsilon_a$. If $0\notin B$ and relative tolerance was
  requested, the evaluator may also report `relative_certified: true` only when
  $\operatorname{rad}(B)/d(B,0)\le\varepsilon_r$.
- `inconclusive`: the procedure exhausted a finite cap before its requested
  enclosure test passed.
- `domain`: the input is outside the stated branch domain, violates a stated
  parameter condition, or lies on a branch cut excluded by that branch.
- `range`: a certified finite enclosure cannot be represented in the requested
  output format; the procedure returns no unsound finite interval.

If a success enclosure contains $0$, it still supplies the stated absolute
bound, but it carries no relative-accuracy claim. The work and precision caps
do not imply that success occurs for every input.

items.title: Fresnel, error, and Gauss hypergeometric series

references.title: N. M. Temme, “Numerical aspects of special functions,” Acta Numerica 17 (2008), §2

items.statement:
For $z\in\mathbb C$, define the Fresnel functions and error function by

$$C(z)=\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\frac{(-1)^k(\pi/2)^{2k}z^{4k+1}}{(2k)!(4k+1)}, \qquad S(z)=\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\frac{(-1)^k(\pi/2)^{2k+1}z^{4k+3}}{(2k+1)!(4k+3)}, \qquad \operatorname{erf}(z)=\frac{2}{\sqrt\pi}\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\frac{(-1)^kz^{2k+1}}{k!(2k+1)}, \qquad \operatorname{erfc}(z)=1-\operatorname{erf}(z).$$

The following local lemmas prove convergence and show that $C,S,\operatorname{erf}$
equal the standard entire integral functions with their usual normalizations.

For $a,b,c,z\in\mathbb C$ with $c\notin\{0,-1,-2,\ldots\}$ and $|z|<1$,
define

$$(a)_0=1,\qquad (a)_k=\prod_{j=0}^{k-1}(a+j),\qquad {}_2F_1(a,b;c;z)=\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\frac{(a)_k(b)_k}{(c)_k k!}z^k.$$

Only this Gauss-series branch of ${}_2F_1$ is defined on this page; no value
outside $|z|<1$ or across a continuation cut is implicit.

items.title: Integer-order Bessel series

references.title: N. M. Temme, “Numerical aspects of special functions,” Acta Numerica 17 (2008), §§2 and 4

items.statement:
For an integer $n\ge0$ and $z\in\mathbb C$, define

$$J_n(z)=\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\frac{(-1)^k(z/2)^{2k+n}}{k!(k+n)!}, \qquad I_n(z)=\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\frac{(z/2)^{2k+n}}{k!(k+n)!}.$$

These are the integer-order Bessel and modified Bessel functions used on this
page. For real $x\ge0$, the scaled modified Bessel value means
$I_n^{\mathrm{sc}}(x)=e^{-x}I_n(x)$. This notation does not assert a finite
evaluation method or a truncation bound; those are proved separately.

items.title: Log-Gamma branch on the right half-plane

references.title: N. M. Temme, “Numerical aspects of special functions,” Acta Numerica 17 (2008), §§2 and 3

items.statement:
On $\operatorname{Re}z>0$, define

$$\ell_+(z)=-\operatorname{Log}z-\gamma_Ez+ \sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\left(\frac zn-\operatorname{Log}\left(1+\frac zn\right)\right).$$

Here $\operatorname{Log}$ is the principal logarithm from
[[def-complex-logarithms-principal-logarithm-and-complex-powers]], and
$\gamma_E$ denotes Euler's constant $\gamma$ from
[[def-euler-mascheroni-constant]]. Both $z$ and $1+z/n$ lie in the
principal-logarithm domain. The local uniform convergence of this series
and the identity $e^{\ell_+(z)}=\Gamma(z)$ are established by
[[lem-loggamma-series-convergence-and-gamma-identity]].

items.title: Finite harmonic enclosure for Euler's constant

references.title: N. M. Temme, “Numerical aspects of special functions,” Acta Numerica 17 (2008), §§2 and 3

items.statement:
For each integer $M\ge1$, put $H_M=\sum_{k=1}^M1/k$. Euler's constant
$\gamma$ satisfies
$$0\le H_M-\log M-\gamma\le\frac1M.$$
Thus $[H_M-\log M-1/M,\ H_M-\log M]$ is a finite enclosure for $\gamma$.

items.title: Gamma functional equation away from the poles

references.title: N. M. Temme, “Numerical aspects of special functions,” Acta Numerica 17 (2008), §§2 and 3

items.statement:
For every $z\in\mathbb C\setminus\{0,-1,-2,\ldots\}$,
$$\Gamma(z+1)=z\Gamma(z),$$
where $\Gamma$ is the meromorphic continuation of Euler's Gamma function.

items.title: Spherical Bessel and outgoing Hankel function conventions
items.statement:
For real $z>0$, let $D_z:=z^{-1}\frac{d}{dz}$ and define, for integers $\ell\ge0$,
$$j_\ell(z):=(-z)^\ell D_z^\ell\left(\frac{\sin z}{z}\right),\qquad h_\ell^{(1)}(z):=(-z)^\ell D_z^\ell\left(-i\frac{e^{iz}}{z}\right).$$
The definition fixes the outgoing $e^{iz}$ convention. The functions solve the radial Helmholtz equation and have the recurrence, origin, Wronskian, and infinity behavior by [[lem-spherical-bessel-and-hankel-radial-solutions]].

These symbolic definitions assert no stable or certified numerical evaluation algorithm for large $\ell$ or $z$.
items.axiom_use: No axiom is used. These are exact symbolic functions; no stable or certified evaluation algorithm is asserted.

items.title: Complementary solution for the integer Bessel recurrence

references.title: N. M. Temme, “Numerical aspects of special functions,” Acta Numerica 17 (2008), §§2 and 4

items.statement:
Fix real $x>0$. Let $D_0(x)=-J_1(x)$ and $D_1(x)=J_0(x)$, and for every integer
$j\ge1$ define

$$D_{j+1}(x)=\frac{2j}{x}D_j(x)-D_{j-1}(x).$$

Thus $D$ is the second sequence obtained from the same order recurrence as
$J_j(x)$. It is a local auxiliary solution, not the Bessel function of the
second kind.

items.title: Scaled complementary error function and its moments

references.title: N. M. Temme, “Numerical aspects of special functions,” Acta Numerica 17 (2008), §§3 and 5

items.statement:
For real $x>0$, define
$\operatorname{erfcx}(x)=e^{x^2}\operatorname{erfc}(x)$. For each integer
$k\ge0$, define the finite positive moment

$$M_k(x)=\int_0^\infty t^k e^{-t^2-2xt}\,dt.$$

The moments are auxiliary quantities for a finite-depth interval enclosure of
$\operatorname{erfcx}$. They are not the modified Bessel functions $I_k$.

items.title: Log-Gamma branch on the slit plane

references.title: DLMF, §5.8, analytic continuation and Weierstrass product
N. M. Temme, “Numerical aspects of special functions,” Acta Numerica 17 (2008), §§2 and 3

items.statement:
Let $\Omega=\mathbb C\setminus(-\infty,0]$. For every $z\in\Omega$, an
admissible integer $m\ge0$ with $\operatorname{Re}(z+m)>0$ exists by the
Archimedean property [[lem-archimedean-property-from-completeness]]. Choose
any such $m$ and set

$$\ell(z)=\ell_+(z+m)-\sum_{j=0}^{m-1}\operatorname{Log}(z+j),$$

where the sum is empty if $m=0$ and $\ell_+$ and $\operatorname{Log}$ are
defined in [[def-loggamma-right-halfplane-branch]]. The next lemma proves that
this value is independent of the admissible $m$ and satisfies
$e^{\ell(z)}=\Gamma(z)$.
This is a continued branch of log-Gamma, not a separate principal
$\operatorname{Log}(\Gamma(z))$.

items.title: Airy coefficient recurrence and geometric tail bounds

references.title: N. M. Temme, “Numerical aspects of special functions,” Acta Numerica 17 (2008), §2

items.statement:
The coefficient recurrence in [[def-airy-initial-value-series]] makes both
series solve $y''=zy$. In a residue class $k\equiv r\pmod 3$, successive
nonzero terms have absolute ratio

$$\frac{|z|^3}{(k+3)(k+2)}.$$

If the ratio of each term after a chosen first omitted term is bounded by
$q<1$, that class's tail is at most the first omitted term's absolute value
divided by $1-q$. The series and their first two derivative series converge
locally uniformly on $\mathbb C$.

items.title: Error-function series geometric tail bound

references.title: N. M. Temme, “Numerical aspects of special functions,” Acta Numerica 17 (2008), §2

items.statement:
For the $k$th term $e_k$ of the $\operatorname{erf}$ series in
[[def-fresnel-erf-and-hypergeometric-series]],

$$\frac{|e_{k+1}|}{|e_k|} =\frac{|z|^2}{k+1}\frac{2k+1}{2k+3} \le\frac{|z|^2}{k+1}.$$

The displayed quotient is asserted when $e_k\ne0$. At $z=0$, every $e_k=0$, so the series and every tail are zero; the corresponding division-free inequality $|e_{k+1}|\le |z|^2|e_k|/(k+1)$ holds there as well.

Thus, if $|z|^2/(K+2)=q<1$, the tail after terms $0,\ldots,K$ is bounded by
$|e_{K+1}|/(1-q)$. The series converges locally uniformly. For every
piecewise-$C^1$ path $\gamma:[0,1]\to\mathbb C$ with $\gamma(0)=0$ and
$\gamma(1)=z$, it equals
$$\frac{2}{\sqrt\pi}\int_\gamma e^{-t^2}\,dt,$$
where the complex line integral is defined by
[[def-complex-line-integral-over-a-rectifiable-path]]. In particular, the
straight-segment integral has this value, and the integral is path-independent.

items.title: Fresnel series geometric tail bounds

references.title: N. M. Temme, “Numerical aspects of special functions,” Acta Numerica 17 (2008), §2

items.statement:
For the terms $c_k$ of $C$ and $s_k$ of $S$ in
[[def-fresnel-erf-and-hypergeometric-series]],

$$\frac{|c_{k+1}|}{|c_k|}\le \frac{\pi^2|z|^4/4}{(2k+1)(2k+2)}, \qquad \frac{|s_{k+1}|}{|s_k|}\le \frac{\pi^2|z|^4/4}{(2k+2)(2k+3)}.$$

Each displayed quotient is asserted only when its denominator is nonzero. At $z=0$, every $c_k=s_k=0$, so both series and every tail are zero. The corresponding division-free inequalities obtained by multiplying by $|c_k|$ or $|s_k|$ hold for every $z$.

Once the applicable bound is at most $q<1$ for all terms after a first
omitted term, the absolute tail is bounded by that term divided by $1-q$.
Both series converge locally uniformly on $\mathbb C$. For every
piecewise-$C^1$ path $\gamma:[0,1]\to\mathbb C$ with $\gamma(0)=0$ and
$\gamma(1)=z$, they equal
$$C(z)=\int_\gamma\cos(\pi t^2/2)\,dt,\qquad S(z)=\int_\gamma\sin(\pi t^2/2)\,dt,$$
where the complex line integral is defined by
[[def-complex-line-integral-over-a-rectifiable-path]]. In particular, these
integrals are path-independent and agree with the straight-segment integrals.

items.title: Gauss hypergeometric series geometric tail bound

references.title: N. M. Temme, “Numerical aspects of special functions,” Acta Numerica 17 (2008), §2

items.statement:
Let $a,b,c,z\in\mathbb C$, $|z|<1$, and
$c\notin\{0,-1,-2,\ldots\}$. If $z=0$, then $h_0=1$ and $h_k=0$ for
$k\ge1$, so the series equals $1$ and every tail after $h_0$ is zero.
Suppose instead that $z\ne0$ and neither $a$ nor $b$ is a nonpositive
integer. Then every term $h_k=(a)_k(b)_kz^k/((c)_kk!)$ is nonzero, and for
any integer $N>|c|$,

$$\frac{|h_{k+1}|}{|h_k|} =|z|\frac{|a+k||b+k|}{|c+k|(k+1)} \le q_N:=|z|\frac{(1+|a|/N)(1+|b|/N)}{1-|c|/N} \qquad(k\ge N).$$

For sufficiently large $N$, $q_N<1$; then the tail starting at $h_N$ is at
most $|h_N|/(1-q_N)$. If $a$ or $b$ is a nonpositive integer, the series
terminates and its tail after the last nonzero term is zero.

items.title: Convergence and geometric tails for integer-order Bessel series

references.title: N. M. Temme, “Numerical aspects of special functions,” Acta Numerica 17 (2008), §§2 and 4

items.statement:
For $n\ge0$, $z\ne0$, and either series in
[[def-integer-order-bessel-series]], the absolute term ratio is

$$r_k=\frac{|z|^2}{4(k+1)(k+n+1)}.$$

At $z=0$, the order-zero series have only the constant term $a_0=1$ and
positive orders have only zero terms; in every case the tail after terms
$k=0,\ldots,K$ is zero. The series for $J_n$ and $I_n$ converge absolutely
and locally uniformly in $z\in\mathbb C$. If $K\ge0$ and
$q=|z|^2/[4(K+2)(K+n+2)]<1$, then the tail after terms $k=0,\ldots,K$ has
absolute value at most $|a_{K+1}|/(1-q)$, where $a_k$ is the corresponding
series term. The first two formal termwise derivative series also converge
locally uniformly.

items.title: Weierstrass log-Gamma series converges to a Gamma branch

references.title: DLMF, §5.2, Gamma function and Euler constant
N. M. Temme, “Numerical aspects of special functions,” Acta Numerica 17 (2008), §§2 and 3

items.statement:
For every $z$ with $\operatorname{Re}z>0$, the series defining
$\ell_+(z)$ in [[def-loggamma-right-halfplane-branch]] converges locally
uniformly, defines a holomorphic function, and satisfies
$e^{\ell_+(z)}=\Gamma(z)$ for Euler's Gamma function on that half-plane.

items.title: Spherical Bessel and outgoing Hankel recurrences solve the radial Helmholtz equation
items.statement:
For the functions of [[def-spherical-bessel-and-hankel-functions]], define
$$L_\ell y:=y''+\frac2z y'+\left(1-\frac{\ell(\ell+1)}{z^2}\right)y\qquad(z>0).$$
Then $L_\ell j_\ell=L_\ell h_\ell^{(1)}=0$, and for $y=j,h^{(1)}$,
$$y_{\ell+1}(z)=\frac{\ell}{z}y_\ell(z)-y_\ell'(z),\qquad y_\ell'(z)=y_{\ell-1}(z)-\frac{\ell+1}{z}y_\ell(z)\quad(\ell\ge1).$$
The regular-origin and outgoing-infinity normalizations are
$$j_\ell(z)=\frac{z^\ell}{(2\ell+1)!!}+O(z^{\ell+2}),\quad h_\ell^{(1)}(z)=-i(2\ell-1)!!z^{-\ell-1}(1+O(z))\quad(z\downarrow0),$$
$$j_\ell(z)=\frac{\sin(z-\ell\pi/2)}z+O(z^{-2}),\quad h_\ell^{(1)}(z)=(-i)^{\ell+1}\frac{e^{iz}}z+O(z^{-2})\quad(z\to\infty),$$
where $(-1)!!:=1$. Their Wronskian is
$$j_\ell(z)(h_\ell^{(1)})'(z)-j_\ell'(z)h_\ell^{(1)}(z)=\frac{i}{z^2}.$$
items.axiom_use: The proof uses finite differentiation and power-series algebra only; it makes no certified numerical evaluation claim.

items.statement:
Let $\ell\ge0$ be an integer and $z>0$ real. Put
$$c_\ell=(2\ell+1)!!=\prod_{r=0}^{\ell}(2r+1),\qquad d_\ell=(2\ell-1)!!=\prod_{r=1}^{\ell}(2r-1),$$
where the second product is empty and equals $1$ when $\ell=0$. Using the outgoing convention of [[def-spherical-bessel-and-hankel-functions]], define
$$J_\ell^{\rm sc}(z)=c_\ell z^{-\ell}j_\ell(z),\qquad D J_\ell^{\rm sc}(z)=c_\ell z^{-\ell}j_\ell'(z),$$
$$H_\ell^{\rm sc}(z)=d_\ell^{-1}z^{\ell+1}e^{-iz}h_\ell^{(1)}(z),\qquad D H_\ell^{\rm sc}(z)=d_\ell^{-1}z^{\ell+1}e^{-iz}(h_\ell^{(1)})'(z).$$
The symbols $D J_\ell^{\rm sc}$ and $D H_\ell^{\rm sc}$ mean the scaled derivatives of the original functions, not derivatives of the scaled functions. The available targets are $j_\ell$, $j_\ell'$, $h_\ell^{(1)}$, $(h_\ell^{(1)})'$, and these four scaled quantities; every derivative is with respect to $z$.

An input is either (i) a closed dyadic interval $I=[a,b]\subset(0,\infty)$, requesting an enclosure of the whole target image on $I$, or (ii) a positive real $z$ supplied by an interface that, on each integer request $n\ge1$, terminates and returns a closed dyadic interval $I_n$ containing $z$ with width at most $2^{-n}$. The intervals need not be nested. This is a representation hypothesis on a supplied input, not a claim that every positive real has such a representation. An exact positive dyadic point is the constant-interface case $I_n=[z,z]$. A represented point need not be dyadic: arguments such as $kR$ or $\sqrt{k^2+V_0}R$ are admitted when a caller constructs a terminating interface by rigorous interval propagation from represented parameters. Each returned box must contain the exact composed argument; a midpoint or approximate point alone is not an admissible interface. The caller's construction must retain positivity and prove termination of every requested refinement.

For each target, outputs and optional relative tests use [[def-certified-evaluation-result-contract]]: a real enclosure is an interval, a complex enclosure is a rectangle, and its radius is half its length or half its Euclidean diagonal, respectively. Each target has an exact positive rational absolute tolerance $\varepsilon_a$; an exact positive rational relative tolerance $\varepsilon_r$ may also be requested. A relative flag may be true only when the returned enclosure excludes zero and $\operatorname{rad}(B)/d(B,0)\le\varepsilon_r$. No relative flag is available when the enclosure contains zero.

Intermediate interval endpoints may be exact rationals. Final endpoints are rounded outward to multiples of $2^{-p}$ for an integer $p\ge0$. The mathematical procedure has no fixed exponent limit. A concrete bounded implementation must return `range` or `inconclusive` rather than claim a finite result it cannot represent. Finite caps are specified by the evaluating algorithm. A fixed nondegenerate input interval requests its whole image and is not promised arbitrarily small radius; eventual absolute success is asserted separately for represented-point inputs.

items.title: Finite certified power-series evaluation for Fresnel, erf, and Gauss functions

references.title: N. M. Temme, “Numerical aspects of special functions,” Acta Numerica 17 (2008), §2

items.statement:
Inputs are a target label $T\in\{C,S,\operatorname{erf},{}_2F_1\}$, an exact
dyadic complex argument $z$, and, for the Gauss-series target, exact dyadic
complex parameters $a,b,c$. Also input positive exact rational absolute
tolerance $\varepsilon_a$, optional positive exact rational relative
tolerance $\varepsilon_r$, a fixed exponent range $(e_{\min},e_{\max})$,
and finite positive integer caps $S_{\max},N_{\max},p_{\max},W$, with
$p_{\max}\ge2$. The stage
cap $S_{\max}$ bounds retries, $N_{\max}$ bounds series terms, $p_{\max}$
bounds dyadic precision, and $W$ bounds this procedure's exact interval
operations, term constructions, and elementary-DAG node operations. Every
nested elementary-range call shares this counter and is interrupted with
inconclusive before its next operation would exceed the remaining budget. At
stage $q$, use
precision $p=\max(2,\min(q,p_{\max}))$ and truncation index $q$ for every
elementary-range subcall.

Reject an invalid target, nonpositive tolerance, invalid cap, invalid exponent
range $e_{\min}>e_{\max}$, or a Gauss input with
$|z|^2\ge1$ or $c\in\{0,-1,-2,\ldots\}$ by returning domain. The
Fresnel and error-function branches accept every finite complex $z$.
Outputs are a finite interval or rectangle with status success, or a
status inconclusive, domain, or range as in
[[def-certified-evaluation-result-contract]].

All rational and interval arithmetic uses
[[def-outward-rounded-interval-and-ball-operations]]. Embed real coefficient intervals $X$ as $X+i[0,0]$ in complex arithmetic; typed elementary DAG nodes never use an implicit real-to-complex conversion. If a required
intermediate operation or output endpoint overflows its selected format,
return range. If an elementary-range subcall returns a non-finite status,
skip the current candidate; if no later stage succeeds, return inconclusive.
The same candidate-skip rule applies to every other non-finite arithmetic
status, including split-domain or entire when a rounded divisor contains
zero; never use such a status as a finite interval.
Charge each exact arithmetic operation, coefficient term, rounding, and
elementary-range call against $W$; before an operation that would exceed
$W$, return inconclusive.

At each stage, form $P_q$, a certified dyadic interval containing $\pi$,
only when $T\in\{C,S,\operatorname{erf}\}$. For $r\in\{1/5,1/239\}$, form
$A_q(r)=\sum_{j=0}^{q-1}(-1)^jr^{2j+1}/(2j+1)$ and
$E_q(r)=r^{2q+1}/((2q+1)(1-r^2))$ by exact rational arithmetic. The
arctangent series and geometric-tail argument in
[[lem-range-reduced-exp-log-and-arctan-series-enclosures]]
gives $\arctan r\in[A_q(r)-E_q(r),A_q(r)+E_q(r)]$. Combine these intervals
as $16\arctan(1/5)-4\arctan(1/239)$, then round the resulting endpoints
outward to the selected format at precision $p$. The Machin identity in
[[lem-trigonometric-identities-machin-and-range-reduction]] proves $\pi\in P_q$. If this conversion is non-finite,
skip this stage for the selected Fresnel or erf target. For the Gauss-series
target, omit $P_q$ and all square-root calls.

Only when $T=\operatorname{erf}$, call
[[alg-certified-elementary-range-evaluation]] on the one-node real DAG
$\sqrt{P_q}$ with the same exponent range and precision $p$, and truncation
index $q$. If it returns a finite interval $R_q$, continue only if
$\inf R_q>0$; otherwise skip this stage. This call encloses $\sqrt\pi$
by [[thm-real-elementary-range-enclosures]]. The $C,S$ branches use $P_q$
directly and do not call square root. For a complex rectangle
$B=X+iY$, write
$M(B)=\max(|\inf X|,|\sup X|)+\max(|\inf Y|,|\sup Y|)$; this rational
quantity bounds the modulus of every point in $B$.

At each stage $q=1,\ldots,\min(S_{\max},N_{\max},p_{\max})$, form the
following candidate for the selected target.

- For $C$, sum its defining terms $c_0,\ldots,c_{q-1}$ from
  [[def-fresnel-erf-and-hypergeometric-series]] by interval arithmetic,
  using $P_q/2$ for $\pi/2$. Let $c_q$ be the first omitted term and set
  $$r_C=\frac{(\sup P_q)^2 M(z)^4}{4(2q+1)(2q+2)}.$$
  If $r_C<1$, enlarge the partial-sum rectangle in both coordinates by
  $M(c_q)/(1-r_C)$; otherwise skip this stage.
- For $S$, sum its first $q$ defining terms using $P_q/2$, let $s_q$
  be the first omitted term, and set
  $$r_S=\frac{(\sup P_q)^2 M(z)^4}{4(2q+2)(2q+3)}.$$
  If $r_S<1$, enlarge the partial-sum rectangle in both coordinates by
  $M(s_q)/(1-r_S)$; otherwise skip this stage.
- For erf, use the interval $2/R_q$ from the single square-root call above
  for $2/\sqrt\pi$,
  sum the first $q$ defining terms, and let $e_q$ be the first omitted
  term. Set $r_E=M(z)^2/(q+1)$. If $r_E<1$, enlarge the partial-sum
  rectangle in both coordinates by $M(e_q)/(1-r_E)$; otherwise skip this
  stage.
- For the Gauss series, compute its terms by $h_0=1$ and
  $$h_{k+1}=h_k\,z\,\frac{(a+k)(b+k)}{(c+k)(k+1)}$$
  using outward interval operations. The exact $c+k$ is nonzero by the
  domain check, but its rounded enclosure may contain zero; in that case
  skip this candidate before division. If $a$ or $b$ is a nonpositive integer, let $L$ be one
  more than the smaller absolute value of those nonpositive integer
  parameters. If $L\le q$, sum exactly through $h_{L-1}$ and use zero
  tail. Otherwise put
  $$A=|\Re a|+|\Im a|,\quad B=|\Re b|+|\Im b|,\quad C_0=|\Re c|+|\Im c|,\quad Z_0=|\Re z|+|\Im z|,$$
  If $q\le C_0$, skip this stage before forming a quotient. Otherwise set
  $$r_H=Z_0\frac{(1+A/q)(1+B/q)}{1-C_0/q}.$$
  If $r_H<1$, sum $h_0,\ldots,h_{q-1}$, let $h_q$
  be the first omitted term, and enlarge the partial-sum rectangle in both
  coordinates by $M(h_q)/(1-r_H)$; otherwise skip this stage. The geometric
  bound in [[lem-gauss-hypergeometric-series-geometric-tail]] applies because
  $A,B,C_0,Z_0$ dominate the corresponding complex moduli.

Round each candidate's final endpoints outward to precision $p$. Return
success at the first stage where its radius is at most $\varepsilon_a$.
If relative tolerance was requested, set relative_certified to true exactly
when zero is excluded and the contract's relative-radius inequality holds;
failure of that relative test does not prevent absolute success. If no stage
produces a passing candidate, return inconclusive. The finite stage loop and
the finite elementary-range calls define the procedure completely.

items.title: The Airy Ai function has a negative real zero

references.title: DLMF, §9.9(i), real zeros of Airy functions
N. M. Temme, “Numerical aspects of special functions,” Acta Numerica 17 (2008), §2

items.statement:
The real Airy function $\operatorname{Ai}$ has at least one zero on the
negative real axis.

items.title: Integral representations and a range bound for integer Bessel functions

references.title: DLMF, §10.32(i), integral representations for modified Bessel functions
N. M. Temme, “Numerical aspects of special functions,” Acta Numerica 17 (2008), §§2 and 4

items.statement:
For integer $n\ge0$ and real $x$, the series in
[[def-integer-order-bessel-series]] satisfy

$$J_n(x)=\frac1\pi\int_0^\pi\cos(n\theta-x\sin\theta)\,d\theta, \qquad I_n(x)=\frac1\pi\int_0^\pi e^{x\cos\theta}\cos(n\theta)\,d\theta.$$

Consequently, for $x\ge0$,
$0\le e^{-x}I_n(x)\le1$.

items.title: Binet integral identity for the right-half-plane log-Gamma branch

references.title: DLMF, §5.9(i), Binet's integral representation
references.locator: §5.9(i), equation 5.9.10_2, an alternative Binet integral representation.

references.title: N. M. Temme, “Numerical aspects of special functions,” Acta Numerica 17 (2008), §§2 and 3

items.statement:
For $\operatorname{Re}z>0$, let $\ell_+(z)$ be the branch in
[[def-loggamma-right-halfplane-branch]]. Define
$$\Phi(u)=\int_0^u\bigl(\lfloor v\rfloor-v+1/2\bigr)\,dv.$$
Then the absolutely convergent integral satisfies
$$\ell_+(z)=\left(z-\frac12\right)\operatorname{Log}z-z+ \frac12\log(2\pi)+\int_0^\infty\frac{\Phi(u)}{(u+z)^2}\,du.$$
On each unit interval, $\Phi(n+t)=t(1-t)/2$ for $0\le t\le1$; hence
$0\le\Phi(u)\le1/8$.

items.title: Moment recurrence for the scaled complementary error function

references.title: N. M. Temme, “Numerical aspects of special functions,” Acta Numerica 17 (2008), §§3 and 5

items.statement:
For $x>0$ and integer $k\ge0$, the moments in
[[def-erfcx-moment-sequence]] are finite and positive. They satisfy

$$2xM_0+2M_1=1, \qquad kM_{k-1}=2xM_k+2M_{k+1}\quad(k\ge1).$$

With $r_k=M_{k+1}/M_k$, it follows that

$$r_k=\frac{k+1}{2(x+r_{k+1})},\qquad 0<r_k<\frac{k+1}{2x},\qquad \operatorname{erfcx}(x)=\frac{1}{\sqrt\pi(x+r_0)}.$$

items.title: Bessel differential equations and order recurrences from the series

references.title: N. M. Temme, “Numerical aspects of special functions,” Acta Numerica 17 (2008), §§2 and 4

items.statement:
For $z\ne0$, the functions in [[def-integer-order-bessel-series]] satisfy

$$z^2J_n''+zJ_n'+(z^2-n^2)J_n=0, \qquad z^2I_n''+zI_n'-(z^2+n^2)I_n=0.$$

For real or complex $z\ne0$ and integer $n\ge1$, they also satisfy

$$J_{n-1}(z)+J_{n+1}(z)=\frac{2n}{z}J_n(z), \qquad I_{n-1}(z)-I_{n+1}(z)=\frac{2n}{z}I_n(z).$$

In addition, $J_0'(z)=-J_1(z)$.

At $z=0$, the series limits are $J_0(0)=I_0(0)=1$ and
$J_n(0)=I_n(0)=0$ for $n\ge1$.

items.title: Explicit tail bound for the log-Gamma product series

references.title: N. M. Temme, “Numerical aspects of special functions,” Acta Numerica 17 (2008), §§2 and 3

items.statement:
For $\operatorname{Re}z>0$ and integer $N>2|z|$, the tail in the series for
$\ell_+(z)$ after its first $N$ summands satisfies

$$\left|\sum_{n=N+1}^{\infty} \left(\frac zn-\operatorname{Log}\left(1+\frac zn\right)\right)\right| \le \frac{|z|^2}{2N\left(1-|z|/(N+1)\right)}.$$

items.title: Shifted log-Gamma branch is independent of the shift

references.title: N. M. Temme, “Numerical aspects of special functions,” Acta Numerica 17 (2008), §§2 and 3

items.statement:
For every $z\in\Omega=\mathbb C\setminus(-\infty,0]$, the value $\ell(z)$ in
[[def-loggamma-slit-plane-branch]] is independent of the integer $m\ge0$ with
$\operatorname{Re}(z+m)>0$, is holomorphic on $\Omega$, and satisfies
$e^{\ell(z)}=\Gamma(z)$.

items.title: Finite exact-interval evaluation of scaled spherical Bessel values

references.title: NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions, §10.49, Explicit Formulas
references.locator: §10.49(i), equations 10.49.1–10.49.6, terminating Laurent formulas for spherical Bessel and Hankel functions.

references.title: NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions, §10.74, Methods of Computation
references.locator: §10.74(i), exact spherical formulas and the cancellation risk when |z| is not large compared with the squared order.

references.title: University of Toronto, Lecture Notes on Mathematical Methods 2019–20
references.locator: §6.4, printed pp. 157–158, finite-derivative spherical formula and outgoing Hankel convention.

items.statement:
Inputs are those of [[def-spherical-bessel-evaluation-contract]], a nonempty finite list of valid targets, finite exact positive rational absolute tolerances, optional exact positive rational relative tolerances, and finite integer caps $W,Q,M_{\max},p_{\max}\ge1$. $W$ is the maximum exact-arithmetic work count, $Q$ the maximum stage and represented-point interface index, $M_{\max}$ the maximum Taylor degree, and $p_{\max}$ the maximum final dyadic precision. A Gaussian rational is $a+ib$ with $a,b\in\mathbb Q$. A Laurent polynomial is a finite sum $\sum_k a_k z^k$ with integer exponents and Gaussian-rational coefficients; its formal derivative uses $(z^k)'=kz^{k-1}$. An expression graph below is a finite directed acyclic graph of exact rational arithmetic operations.

Factorials are those of [[def-factorial-and-falling-factorial]]; they are nonzero by that definition and [[lem-of-naturals-positive]], so every displayed factorial denominator is defined. For a rational $x$, $\lceil x\rceil$ denotes the least integer greater than or equal to $x$, computed by exact integer division.

Reject an invalid order, target, tolerance, cap, or interval input not contained in $(0,\infty)$ with `domain`. For a represented point, an interval returned by the input interface may meet zero; such a stage is skipped and a later interface index is tried.

Construct Laurent polynomials by
$$A_0=0,\quad B_0=z^{-1},\quad C_0=-iz^{-1},$$
$$A_{r+1}=rz^{-1}A_r-A_r'-B_r,\quad B_{r+1}=rz^{-1}B_r-B_r'+A_r,\quad C_{r+1}=rz^{-1}C_r-C_r'-iC_r$$
for $r=0,\ldots,\ell-1$. With $s$ and $c$ denoting the sine and cosine input enclosures, form the unscaled outputs
$$u=A_\ell c+B_\ell s,\quad v=(A_\ell'+B_\ell)c+(B_\ell'-A_\ell)s,\quad w=C_\ell(c+is),\quad t=(C_\ell'+iC_\ell)(c+is).$$
Form the scaled outputs
$$c_\ell z^{-\ell}u,\quad c_\ell z^{-\ell}v,\quad d_\ell^{-1}z^{\ell+1}C_\ell,\quad d_\ell^{-1}z^{\ell+1}(C_\ell'+iC_\ell).$$
Collect like Laurent powers exactly; in particular cancel negative powers in the scaled $h_\ell^{(1)}$ value when they cancel algebraically. A remaining $z^{-1}$ in the scaled derivative is evaluated only on positive input intervals.

For real intervals use exact rational endpoint hulls: $[a,b]+[c,d]=[a+c,b+d]$, $[a,b][c,d]=[\min(ac,ad,bc,bd),\max(ac,ad,bc,bd)]$, and $[a,b]^{-1}=[1/b,1/a]$ when $0<a\le b$. For complex rectangles, apply these real interval operations to the real and imaginary components of $(x+iy)(u+iv)=(xu-yv)+i(xv+yu)$. Thus interval arithmetic encloses every pointwise sum and product; division is only by a positive power of the positive argument or by a positive integer constant. Compute powers, factorials, and rational endpoints by finite exact arithmetic.

At a positive current box $I=[a,b]$, choose $M\ge0$ with $M+2\ge2b$ and form the rational interval polynomial and rational tail
$$T_M(I)=\sum_{m=0}^{M}\frac{(iI)^m}{m!},\qquad E_M=\frac{2b^{M+1}}{(M+1)!}.$$
The interval power is repeated complex-rectangle multiplication. Enclose $\cos(I)$ by $\operatorname{Re}T_M(I)+[-E_M,E_M]$ and $\sin(I)$ by $\operatorname{Im}T_M(I)+[-E_M,E_M]$. Evaluate each requested output graph with these leaves and $z\in I$, and round each final endpoint outward to the grid $2^{-p}\mathbb Z$.

Use the following deterministic finite search. Charge the Laurent recurrence, graph construction, and coefficient collection to the work counter as they are performed. For stages $q=1,\ldots,Q$, first take the fixed interval unchanged, or call the represented-point interface at index $q$. Skip a represented-point stage unless its returned interval has $a>0$. Set $p=q$ and $M=\max(q,\lceil2b\rceil)$. If $p>p_{\max}$ or $M>M_{\max}$, stop with `inconclusive`. Evaluate all requested graphs and the displayed $T_M,E_M$ using the work counter: each exact rational or Gaussian-rational arithmetic operation or comparison, each Taylor term, each endpoint-rounding operation, and each interface call costs one unit. If the next operation would exceed $W$, stop with `inconclusive` before performing it. If the output format cannot represent a certified endpoint, return `range` with no finite claim. If every requested target has radius at most its absolute tolerance, return `success`; for each optional relative tolerance, set its flag true exactly when the enclosure excludes zero and the relative test in the contract passes. A failed relative test does not prevent absolute `success`. If no stage succeeds before a cap or the search ends, return `inconclusive`. No floating-point recurrence is used.

items.title: Composite midpoint enclosure for the integer Bessel integral

references.title: N. M. Temme, “Numerical aspects of special functions,” Acta Numerica 17 (2008), §§2 and 4

items.statement:
Let $n\ge0$ be an integer, $x\in\mathbb R$, $m\ge1$, and $h=\pi/m$. Put
$\phi(\theta)=\cos(n\theta-x\sin\theta)$ and
$Q_m=h\sum_{j=0}^{m-1}\phi((j+1/2)h)$. Then

$$\left|J_n(x)-\frac{Q_m}{\pi}\right| \le \frac{h^2}{24}\left((n+|x|)^2+|x|\right).$$

This is the local composite-midpoint certificate for the Bessel integral; it
does not certify floating-point summation unless each operation is enclosed.

items.title: Adjacent initial Bessel values cannot both vanish

references.title: N. M. Temme, “Numerical aspects of special functions,” Acta Numerica 17 (2008), §§2 and 4

items.statement: For every real $x>0$, $J_0(x)$ and $J_1(x)$ are not both zero.

items.title: Signed finite remainder for the erfcx asymptotic expansion

references.title: N. M. Temme, “Numerical aspects of special functions,” Acta Numerica 17 (2008), §§3 and 5

items.statement:
For real $x>0$ and integer $N\ge1$, put

$$(1/2)_0=1,\qquad (1/2)_k=\prod_{j=0}^{k-1}(j+1/2).$$

$$S_N(x)=\frac1{x\sqrt\pi}\sum_{k=0}^{N-1} (-1)^k\frac{(1/2)_k}{x^{2k}}.$$

Then

$$\operatorname{erfcx}(x)-S_N(x)=(-1)^N R_N(x),\qquad 0\le R_N(x)\le \frac1{x\sqrt\pi}\frac{(2N)!}{4^N N!x^{2N}}.$$

This is a finite signed remainder bound, not a convergence assertion for the
asymptotic series.

items.title: Finite continued-fraction enclosure for erfcx

references.title: N. M. Temme, “Numerical aspects of special functions,” Acta Numerica 17 (2008), §§3 and 5

items.statement:
Fix real $x>0$ and integer $N\ge0$. Set
$I_N=[0,(N+1)/(2x)]$, and for $k=N-1,\ldots,0$ define

$$I_k=\left[\frac{k+1}{2(x+\sup I_{k+1})}, \frac{k+1}{2(x+\inf I_{k+1})}\right].$$

Then $r_k\in I_k$ for every $0\le k\le N$, where $r_k$ is the moment ratio
from [[lem-erfcx-moment-recurrence]]. Therefore

$$\operatorname{erfcx}(x)\in \left[\frac1{\sqrt\pi(x+\sup I_0)}, \frac1{\sqrt\pi(x+\inf I_0)}\right].$$

Each finite depth gives a valid enclosure; no convergence or shrinking-width
claim as $N$ grows is made.

items.title: Composite midpoint enclosure for the scaled modified Bessel integral

references.title: DLMF, §10.32(ii), integral representations for modified Bessel functions
N. M. Temme, “Numerical aspects of special functions,” Acta Numerica 17 (2008), §§2 and 4

items.statement:
Let $n\ge0$ be an integer, $x\ge0$, $m\ge1$, $h=\pi/m$, and
$$f(\theta)=e^{-x(1-\cos\theta)}\cos(n\theta),\qquad Q_m=h\sum_{j=0}^{m-1}f((j+1/2)h).$$
Then
$$\left|e^{-x}I_n(x)-\frac{Q_m}{\pi}\right| \le \frac{h^2}{24}\bigl((x+n)^2+x\bigr).$$
The bound certifies the exact midpoint integral. Floating-point summation is
certified only if its operations are enclosed separately.

items.title: Explicit sectorial remainder bound for the right-half-plane log-Gamma branch

references.title: DLMF, §5.9(i), Binet's integral representations
references.locator: Equation 5.9.10_2, an alternative Binet integral representation.

references.title: DLMF, §5.11(i), Stirling's expansion for log-Gamma
references.locator: Equation 5.11.1, the sectorial log-Gamma Stirling expansion.

references.title: N. M. Temme, “Numerical aspects of special functions,” Acta Numerica 17 (2008), §§2–5

items.statement:
Fix $0<\delta\le\pi/2$ and $z\in\mathbb C$ with $\operatorname{Re}z>0$.
For the branch $\ell_+$ from [[def-loggamma-right-halfplane-branch]],
[[lem-binet-loggamma-right-halfplane-identity]] gives
$$\ell_+(z)=\left(z-\frac12\right)\operatorname{Log}z-z+ \frac12\log(2\pi)+R(z), \qquad R(z)=\int_0^\infty\frac{\Phi(u)}{(u+z)^2}\,du,$$
where $\Phi(u)=\int_0^u(\lfloor v\rfloor-v+1/2)\,dv$. Then
$$|R(z)|\le \frac{1}{8\sin^2(\delta/2)|z|}.$$
For $\delta=\pi/2$, the bound is $1/(4|z|)$. The relative error after
exponentiating the three main terms is at most $\exp(|R(z)|)-1$.

items.title: Soundness of the finite Fresnel, erf, and Gauss-series enclosures

references.title: N. M. Temme, “Numerical aspects of special functions,” Acta Numerica 17 (2008), §2

items.statement:
If [[alg-certified-fresnel-erf-hypergeometric-series]] returns `success` for
$C,S,\operatorname{erf}$, or a Gauss-series value on its stated domain, its
returned interval or rectangle contains that exact function value and passes
the requested absolute-radius test. A relative certificate is valid only when
the enclosure excludes zero and the contract's relative-radius test passes.
Every execution with finite caps terminates. The theorem makes no claim of success for every valid input.

items.title: Soundness and eventual absolute precision for spherical Bessel enclosures
items.statement: Every `success` output of [[alg-certified-scaled-spherical-bessel-evaluation]] encloses each requested scaled or unscaled value, or the entire requested image for an interval input, and satisfies its absolute-radius test. Its relative flags satisfy [[def-certified-evaluation-result-contract]]. Every capped execution terminates. For each fixed order, positive represented real point, finite nonempty target list, and positive rational absolute tolerances, some finite work, degree, interface-index, and precision caps permit absolute success. The same holds for an exact positive dyadic point. For a nonzero requested target, any positive rational relative tolerance can also eventually be certified by rerunning with sufficiently small positive rational absolute tolerances and sufficiently large finite caps; no relative certification is promised at a zero. The theorem gives no uniform floating-point condition number, bit-complexity bound, success guarantee for fixed small caps, or scattering uniqueness result.

items.title: Finite certified evaluation of the scaled complementary error function

references.title: N. M. Temme, “Numerical aspects of special functions,” Acta Numerica 17 (2008), §§3 and 5

items.statement:
Input an exact dyadic real $x$, positive rational absolute tolerance
$\varepsilon_a$, optional positive rational relative tolerance
$\varepsilon_r$, a fixed exponent range $(e_{\min},e_{\max})$, and finite
positive integer caps $S_{\max},D_{\max},N_{\max},p_{\max},W$, with
$p_{\max}\ge2$. Here
$S_{\max}$ bounds stages, $D_{\max}$ the continued-fraction depth,
$N_{\max}$ the asymptotic truncation, $p_{\max}$ the dyadic precision, and
$W$ the exact interval operations, terms, and subroutine calls performed by
this procedure. Reject nonpositive tolerances, invalid caps,
$e_{\min}>e_{\max}$, or $x\le0$ with domain. At stage $q$, use
$D=\min(q,D_{\max})$, $N=\min(q,N_{\max})$, precision
$p=\max(2,\min(q,p_{\max}))$, and truncation index $q$ for elementary-range calls.
Outputs and status meanings are those of
[[def-certified-evaluation-result-contract]].

All rational and interval arithmetic uses
[[def-outward-rounded-interval-and-ball-operations]]. Charge every exact
arithmetic operation, range-evaluator node operation, term, rounding, and
loop update to the shared counter $W$. Interrupt any nested elementary-range
call with inconclusive before its next operation would exceed the remaining
budget. Return inconclusive before any local operation would exceed $W$. A
final endpoint overflow
returns range. A non-finite required arithmetic operation or elementary-range subcall makes its candidate unavailable; if neither candidate can be formed, the current stage is
inconclusive and later stages may still be tried.

For each stage $q=1,\ldots,S_{\max}$, compute $P_q$, a finite dyadic
interval containing $\pi$, as follows. For $r\in\{1/5,1/239\}$, form
$A_q(r)=\sum_{j=0}^{q-1}(-1)^jr^{2j+1}/(2j+1)$ and
$E_q(r)=r^{2q+1}/((2q+1)(1-r^2))$ exactly; the arctangent-tail lemma gives
$\arctan r\in[A_q(r)-E_q(r),A_q(r)+E_q(r)]$. Combine these intervals by
$\pi=16\arctan(1/5)-4\arctan(1/239)$ and round outward to the selected
format at precision $p$. The Machin identity is supplied by
[[lem-trigonometric-identities-machin-and-range-reduction]]; the arctangent
series and its geometric-tail argument are in
[[lem-range-reduced-exp-log-and-arctan-series-enclosures]]. If the interval
conversion is non-finite, skip the stage. Call
[[alg-certified-elementary-range-evaluation]] on the real one-node DAG
$\sqrt{P_q}$, using exponent range $(e_{\min},e_{\max})$, precision $p$,
and truncation $q$. If this call is not finite or its output $R_q$ does
not have positive lower endpoint, skip this stage. Otherwise $R_q$ encloses
$\sqrt\pi$ by [[thm-real-elementary-range-enclosures]].

Form the continued-fraction candidate as follows. Set
$I_D=[0,(D+1)/(2x)]$. For $k=D-1,\ldots,0$, set
$$I_k=\left[\frac{k+1}{2(x+\sup I_{k+1})}, \frac{k+1}{2(x+\inf I_{k+1})}\right]$$
by outward interval operations. Apply the decreasing map
$r\mapsto1/(\sqrt\pi(x+r))$ to $I_0$, evaluating $\sqrt\pi$ with
$R_q$, to obtain a candidate interval $C_q$. The finite-depth
containment lemma [[lem-erfcx-continued-fraction-enclosure]] makes $C_q$
a valid enclosure for every $D\ge0$.

If $N\ge1$, also form the asymptotic candidate. Evaluate
$$S_N(x)=\frac1{x\sqrt\pi}\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}(-1)^k\frac{(1/2)_k}{x^{2k}}, \qquad B_N(x)=\frac1{x\sqrt\pi}\frac{(2N)!}{4^NN!x^{2N}}$$
with $R_q$ and exact factorial/rational interval arithmetic. Write the computed sum interval as $[s_-,s_+]$ and take a nonnegative outward upper endpoint $b_N$ for the remainder bound $B_N$. Set
$A_q=[s_-,s_++b_N]$ when $N$ is even and
$A_q=[s_--b_N,s_+]$ when $N$ is odd, rounding the final endpoints outward. The signed remainder lemma
[[lem-erfcx-asymptotic-remainder]] makes $A_q$ a valid enclosure.

If both candidates are finite, intersect them when the intersection is
nonempty; if it is empty, discard the stage. If only one is finite, use that
candidate. Round the selected final endpoints outward to precision $p$.
Return success at the first stage whose radius is at most
$\varepsilon_a$. Set relative_certified to true exactly when relative
tolerance was requested, the interval excludes zero, and the contract's
relative-radius test passes; a failed relative test does not prevent absolute
success. If no stage passes before the finite caps, return inconclusive.

items.title: Finite certified evaluation of Gamma and a continued log-Gamma branch

references.title: N. M. Temme, “Numerical aspects of special functions,” Acta Numerica 17 (2008), §§2 and 3

items.statement:
Inputs are a finite dyadic complex rectangle $Z$, a target label $\Gamma$ or
$\ell$, positive exact rational absolute tolerance $\varepsilon_a$,
optional positive exact rational relative tolerance $\varepsilon_r$, a fixed
dyadic format precision $p_0\ge2$ and exponent range
$(e_{\min},e_{\max})$, fixed integer elementary truncation index $K\ge1$,
finite positive integer work cap $W$, and integer precision cap $P\ge p_0$.
The target
$\ell$ is the continued
branch in [[def-loggamma-slit-plane-branch]]. Reject an invalid target, empty or non-finite rectangle, invalid cap,
tolerance, $e_{\min}>e_{\max}$, or
$Z\not\subset\mathbb C\setminus(-\infty,0]$ by returning
domain. The exact rectangle test is: either the imaginary interval omits
zero, or the real interval has strictly positive lower endpoint. Reject a
selected shift $m>W$ with inconclusive. For stages $q=1,\ldots,P$, use
precision $p=\max(p_0,q)$, harmonic cutoff $M=\min(q,W)$, product cutoff
$N=\min(q,W)$, and the fixed elementary truncation index $K$ for every
range call. Output statuses are those of
[[def-certified-evaluation-result-contract]].

Use [[def-outward-rounded-interval-and-ball-operations]] for interval
arithmetic. Count every exact rational or interval operation, series term,
elementary-DAG node operation, rounding, and loop update against the shared
counter $W$. If the procedure is called by another evaluator, charge these
same primitive operations directly to that caller's shared counter, so the
caller can debit the actual child work; the local cap $W$ remains in force.
Before any operation would exceed either remaining cap, return inconclusive.
Run nested elementary-range calls under that counter and interrupt a subcall
before its next operation would exceed the remaining budget. A non-finite
range result makes the current candidate unavailable. Any other non-finite arithmetic result also makes its candidate unavailable; no partial result is retained. Final output overflow
returns range.

Choose
$$m=\max\!\left(0,\left\lfloor-\inf\Re Z\right\rfloor+1\right),$$
which is the least integer $m\ge0$ for which $\inf\Re Z+m>0$. Compute
this exactly from the rational endpoint; if $m>W$, return inconclusive
before forming the shift. Put $W_Z=Z+m$.
Before every elementary-range call, round each rational interval input
outward to the stage dyadic format; a conversion overflow makes that candidate
unavailable. A rounded Log input must still avoid the cut; otherwise its candidate is unavailable, rather than declaring the valid original input outside the domain. Embed a real interval $X$ explicitly as $X+i[0,0]$ whenever it participates in a complex expression; real and complex DAG nodes retain their declared types. All elementary-range calls below use
[[alg-certified-elementary-range-evaluation]] with the selected format and
fixed truncation $K$; its soundness for finite real and complex results is
given by
[[thm-real-elementary-range-enclosures]] and
[[thm-complex-elementary-range-enclosures]].

For stage $q=1,\ldots,P$, form a dyadic $P_q$ containing $\pi$:
for $r\in\{1/5,1/239\}$, compute exactly
$A_q(r)=\sum_{k=0}^{q-1}(-1)^kr^{2k+1}/(2k+1)$ and
$E_q(r)=r^{2q+1}/((2q+1)(1-r^2))$, combine
$\arctan r\in[A_q(r)-E_q(r),A_q(r)+E_q(r)]$ by the Machin identity, and
round outward to the selected format at precision $p$. The arctangent
series and its geometric-tail argument are in
[[lem-range-reduced-exp-log-and-arctan-series-enclosures]], and the Machin
identity is in [[lem-trigonometric-identities-machin-and-range-reduction]]. If the conversion
is non-finite or $\inf P_q\le0$, the Stirling candidate is unavailable for
this stage; still attempt the product candidate. Let
$a_W=\inf\Re W_Z>0$ and
$R_W=\max(|\inf\Re W_Z|,|\sup\Re W_Z|)
+\max(|\inf\Im W_Z|,|\sup\Im W_Z|)$; $R_W$ is an exact rational upper
bound for $|w|$ on $W_Z$.

For this stage, call the elementary-range algorithm on the principal-log node
for each $Z+j$, $j=0,\ldots,m-1$. Translation by these real integers
preserves avoidance of the cut for an input rectangle wholly in the slit
plane; if the exact branch-domain check fails, return domain. Add the finite
log rectangles to form the shift sum $L_Z$. If any shift-log call is non-finite, discard this whole stage, since both candidates require that sum. When $m=0$, set $L_Z=0$.

Construct the product candidate when $N>2R_W$. Call the elementary-range
algorithm for the real node $\log M$ to get an enclosure $G_M=[g_-,g_+]$ of
$\log M$, and form the outward-rounded Euler-constant interval
$[H_M-g_+-1/M,\ H_M-g_-]$, where $H_M=\sum_{k=1}^M1/k$ exactly. Call
the complex principal-log node on $W_Z$ and on each $1+W_Z/k$ for
$1\le k\le N$. All these rectangles lie in the principal-log domain since
$\Re W_Z>0$. Form
$$Q_N=-\operatorname{Log}(W_Z)-\gamma_E W_Z+ \sum_{k=1}^N\left(\frac{W_Z}{k}-\operatorname{Log}(1+W_Z/k)\right)$$
by interval arithmetic, and enlarge each coordinate by an outward upper bound for
$$T_N=\frac{R_W^2}{2N(1-R_W/(N+1))}.$$
The tail lemma [[lem-loggamma-product-tail-bound]] proves that this is an
enclosure of $\ell_+(W_Z)$, uniformly on the whole rectangle. Subtract
$L_Z$ to get the shifted product candidate for $\ell(Z)$. If $N\le2R_W$
or a required call is non-finite, this candidate is unavailable at this stage.

Construct the Stirling candidate only when $P_q$ is finite and has positive
lower endpoint. Call the complex principal-log node on $W_Z$, and the real
logarithm node on $2P_q$. Form
$$S_Z=(W_Z-\tfrac12)\operatorname{Log}(W_Z)-W_Z+ \tfrac12\log(2\pi)-L_Z$$
by interval arithmetic and enlarge each coordinate by an outward upper bound for $1/(4a_W)$.
The sectorial remainder lemma [[lem-sectorial-stirling-explicit-remainder-bound]]
proves this is an enclosure of $\ell(Z)$. If a required call is non-finite,
this candidate is unavailable at this stage.

If both log candidates are available, intersect them when the intersection is
nonempty; if empty, discard the stage. If only one is available, select it.
For target $\ell$, use this rectangle as the output candidate. For target
$\Gamma$, call the complex exponential node on the selected rectangle and
use its finite output rectangle. Return success at the first stage whose
candidate radius is at most $\varepsilon_a$. Set relative_certified to true
exactly when relative tolerance was requested, zero is excluded, and the
contract's relative-radius test passes; a failed relative test does not
prevent absolute success. If no stage succeeds before its caps, return
inconclusive.

items.title: Positive discrete Wronskian for the Bessel recurrence pair

references.title: N. M. Temme, “Numerical aspects of special functions,” Acta Numerica 17 (2008), §§2 and 4

items.statement:
Fix real $x>0$, let $J_j(x)$ be as in
[[def-integer-order-bessel-series]], and let $D_j(x)$ be as in
[[def-bessel-complementary-recurrence-solution]]. Define
$W_j=J_jD_{j+1}-J_{j+1}D_j$. Then

$$W_j=J_0(x)^2+J_1(x)^2>0\qquad(j\ge0).$$

In particular, the two recurrence solutions $J$ and $D$ are linearly
independent.

items.title: Exact finite terminal-contamination error identity

references.title: N. M. Temme, “Numerical aspects of special functions,” Acta Numerica 17 (2008), §§2 and 4

items.statement:
Fix $x>0$, integers $N\ge1$ and $0\le n<N$, and define the exact backward
recurrence solution by $u_{N+1}=0$, $u_N=1$, and
$u_{j-1}=2ju_j/x-u_{j+1}$ for $j=N,N-1,\ldots,1$. If
$D_{N+1}(x)\ne0$, put $q=-J_{N+1}(x)/D_{N+1}(x)$. For $s\in\{0,1\}$ such
that $J_s(x)+qD_s(x)\ne0$, let
$\widehat J_n=J_s(x)u_n/u_s$. Then

$$\widehat J_n-J_n= \frac{q\bigl(J_sD_n-J_nD_s\bigr)}{J_s+qD_s}.$$

This is a finite-$N$ identity. It makes no assertion that the error tends to
zero as $N\to\infty$.

items.title: Soundness of finite erfcx enclosures

references.title: N. M. Temme, “Numerical aspects of special functions,” Acta Numerica 17 (2008), §§3 and 5

items.statement:
If [[alg-certified-erfcx-evaluation]] returns `success` for $x>0$, the
returned interval contains $\operatorname{erfcx}(x)$ and passes the requested
absolute-radius test. A relative certificate is valid only if zero is outside
the interval and the required relative-radius test passes. Every execution
with finite caps terminates. The theorem makes no success claim for every
$x$ or finite cap.

items.title: Soundness of finite Gamma and log-Gamma enclosures

references.title: N. M. Temme, “Numerical aspects of special functions,” Acta Numerica 17 (2008), §§2 and 3

items.statement:
For any finite dyadic rectangle $Z\subset\mathbb C\setminus(-\infty,0]$,
whenever [[alg-certified-gamma-loggamma-evaluation]] returns `success`, its
returned enclosure contains the range of $\Gamma$ or the continued log-Gamma
branch on $Z$ and passes the stated absolute-radius test. Any reported
relative certificate obeys the zero-exclusion condition. No assertion
guarantees success for every valid input or finite cap. Every execution with
finite caps terminates.

items.title: Finite certified Airy power-series evaluation

references.title: N. M. Temme, “Numerical aspects of special functions,” Acta Numerica 17 (2008), §2

items.statement:
Inputs are an exact dyadic complex number $z$, a target label
$\operatorname{Ai}$ or $\operatorname{Bi}$, positive rational absolute
tolerance $\varepsilon_a$, optional positive rational relative tolerance
$\varepsilon_r$, a fixed exponent range $(e_{\min},e_{\max})$, and finite
positive integer caps $S_{\max},K_{\max},p_{\max},W$, with $p_{\max}\ge2$.
Reject an invalid target, nonpositive tolerance, invalid cap, or
$e_{\min}>e_{\max}$ with domain. The caps bound stages,
terms per residue class, final dyadic precision, and this procedure's exact
interval operations and subroutine calls. For stage $q$, use $K=q$,
precision $p=\max(2,\min(q,p_{\max}))$, and elementary-range truncation $q$;
run stages $q=1,\ldots,\min(S_{\max},K_{\max},p_{\max})$.

All arithmetic uses [[def-outward-rounded-interval-and-ball-operations]].
Charge every exact arithmetic operation, range-evaluator node operation,
term, rounding, and loop update to the shared counter $W$. Return
inconclusive before any local operation would exceed $W$; interrupt a nested
subroutine before its next operation would exceed the remaining budget. When
nested, charge every Gamma-child operation directly to the same parent counter.
If a final
endpoint overflows, return range. A non-finite subroutine result makes the
current stage unavailable; later stages may still be tried. Other statuses
are those of [[def-certified-evaluation-result-contract]].

At stage $q$, outward-round the rational points $1/3$ and $2/3$ to
dyadic intervals $G_r$ at precision $p$. For each $r\in\{1/3,2/3\}$, charge the
child-call operation to the parent counter. If no parent work unit remains,
return inconclusive; otherwise pass the positive remaining budget as the
child's work cap and call
[[alg-certified-gamma-loggamma-evaluation]] with target $\Gamma$ on the
complex rectangle $G_r+i[0,0]$, absolute tolerance $2^{-q}$, no relative
tolerance, the same exponent range, fixed elementary truncation $q$,
base format precision $p$, and precision cap $p$. Debit every operation
performed by the Gamma child to the shared counter. A
success output rectangle encloses
$\Gamma(r)$, since $r\in G_r$; if either call is not successful or its
rectangle contains zero, skip this stage. A failed rational-to-dyadic conversion also makes the stage unavailable.

For $s\in\{1/6,1/3,2/3\}$, outward-round the exact rational $s$ to a
dyadic interval $S_{s,p}$, then call
[[alg-certified-elementary-range-evaluation]] on the real expression DAG
$\exp(S_{s,p}\log 3)$, with the same exponent range, precision $p$, and
truncation $q$. These calls enclose $3^s$ by
[[thm-real-elementary-range-enclosures]]. If a required call is not finite,
skip this stage. Embed each real power interval $X$ as the complex rectangle $X+i[0,0]$, then combine it with the Gamma rectangles by outward complex arithmetic
to enclose the two initial coefficients
$$(a_0,a_1)=\left(\frac{1}{3^{2/3}\Gamma(2/3)}, -\frac{1}{3^{1/3}\Gamma(1/3)}\right)$$
for Ai, or
$$(b_0,b_1)=\left(\frac{1}{3^{1/6}\Gamma(2/3)}, \frac{3^{1/6}}{\Gamma(1/3)}\right)$$
for Bi. If any divisor rectangle contains zero or an arithmetic operation is non-finite, skip this stage.

Put $R=|\Re z|+|\Im z|$, an exact rational upper bound for $|z|$.
For each residue $r=0,1$, initialize $t_{r,0}=c_r z^r$ using the
selected pair of initial coefficient intervals, and compute
$t_{r,j+1}=t_{r,j}z^3/((k+3)(k+2))$, where $k=r+3j$. Sum
$t_{r,0},\ldots,t_{r,q-1}$ and compute the first omitted term
$t_{r,q}$. Put $k_r=r+3q$ and
$$\rho_r=\frac{R^3}{(k_r+3)(k_r+2)}.$$
If either $\rho_r\ge1$, skip the stage. Otherwise enlarge the sum of both
partial rectangles in each coordinate by
$$\frac{M(t_{0,q})}{1-\rho_0}+\frac{M(t_{1,q})}{1-\rho_1},$$
where $M(X+iY)=\max(|\inf X|,|\sup X|)
+\max(|\inf Y|,|\sup Y|)$. The $c_2=0$ residue class vanishes identically.
The ratio and tail lemma [[lem-airy-series-coefficient-recurrence-and-tail]]
therefore makes the enlarged rectangle a containing enclosure of the selected
Airy value.

Round the final rectangle outward to precision $p$. Return success at the
first stage whose radius is at most $\varepsilon_a$. Set relative_certified
to true exactly when relative tolerance was requested, zero is excluded, and
the contract's relative-radius test passes; a failed relative test does not
prevent absolute success. If no stage succeeds before its caps, return
inconclusive. The stage loop and all subroutine calls have finite caps, so the
procedure has no unbounded retry.

items.title: Finite certified evaluation of integer-order Bessel functions

references.title: DLMF, §10.2, Bessel functions of the first kind
N. M. Temme, “Numerical aspects of special functions,” Acta Numerica 17 (2008), §§2 and 4

items.statement:
Inputs are an integer order $n\ge0$, a target $J$ or scaled $I$, an exact
dyadic real argument $x$, positive rational absolute tolerance
$\varepsilon_a$, optional positive rational relative tolerance
$\varepsilon_r$, a fixed exponent range $(e_{\min},e_{\max})$, and finite
positive integer caps $S_{\max},K_{\max},M_{\max},N_{\max},p_{\max},W$, with
$p_{\max}\ge2$.
The caps bound stages, series terms, midpoint panels, Miller terminal index,
dyadic precision, and exact interval operations and subroutine calls. Run
stages $q=1,\ldots,\min(S_{\max},K_{\max},M_{\max},p_{\max})$, using precision
$p=\max(2,\min(q,p_{\max}))$ and elementary-range truncation $q$. Reject
$n<0$, invalid targets, nonpositive tolerances, invalid caps,
$e_{\min}>e_{\max}$, or $x<0$ for the scaled $I$ target with
domain. The scaled
target is always $e^{-x}I_n(x)$.

Use exact rational endpoint formulas for finite sums, recurrences, mesh
construction, and error bounds, with final endpoints rounded outward to
precision $p$. Charge every exact arithmetic operation, range-evaluator
node operation, term, rounding, and loop update to the shared counter $W$;
interrupt a nested elementary-range call with inconclusive before its next
operation would exceed the remaining budget. Factorials use
[[def-factorial-and-falling-factorial]]. Call
[[alg-certified-elementary-range-evaluation]] for the real sine, cosine, and
exponential ranges in the midpoint branches. Before each call, round its
rational input interval outward to the fixed dyadic format. Its finite outputs are sound by
[[thm-real-elementary-range-enclosures]]. Count each exact operation, term,
rounding, and subroutine call against $W$; if the next operation would
exceed $W$, return inconclusive. A non-finite elementary call makes that
branch unavailable. Final endpoint overflow returns range.

Before forming any stage constant, if the target is scaled $I$ and $x=0$,
use precision $p=p_{\max}$, form $[1,1]$ when $n=0$ and $[0,0]$ when $n\ge1$, and round its
endpoints outward to that format. If either conversion overflows,
return range. Otherwise apply the ordinary absolute-radius test to the rounded candidate and return `success` only when it passes; return `inconclusive` if it fails. The internal exact candidate has radius zero, but outward underflow may widen its stored enclosure. Set a successful output's relative flag by the usual contract test, so a zero value
receives no relative certificate. This branch does not call the
elementary-range procedure.

At stage $q$, compute an outward dyadic interval $P_q$ containing $\pi$
from the Machin identity in
[[lem-trigonometric-identities-machin-and-range-reduction]] and the
arctangent series and geometric-tail argument in
[[lem-range-reduced-exp-log-and-arctan-series-enclosures]]: for
$r=1/5,1/239$, use the $q$-term sum
$\sum_{k=0}^{q-1}(-1)^kr^{2k+1}/(2k+1)$ and tail bound
$r^{2q+1}/((2q+1)(1-r^2))$, combine by $16\arctan(1/5)-4\arctan(1/239)$,
and round outward to the selected format at precision $p$. If this
conversion is non-finite or $\inf P_q\le0$, midpoint candidates are
unavailable at this stage; the independent power-series or Miller branches may
still be attempted.

For a requested $J_n(x)$, first form a power-series candidate if possible.
For any order $r\ge0$, define the finite subroutine $\operatorname{SeriesJ}(r)$:
start
$a_0=(x/2)^r/(0!\,r!)$ and
$a_{k+1}=-a_kx^2/(4(k+1)(k+r+1))$; sum $a_0,\ldots,a_{q-1}$, and
compute $a_q$. Put
$$\rho_J=\frac{x^2}{4(q+1)(q+r+1)}.$$
If $\rho_J<1$, return the interval partial sum enlarged by
$|a_q|/(1-\rho_J)$; otherwise mark this series candidate unavailable.
The tail lemma [[lem-integer-order-bessel-series-tail]] proves each returned
interval contains $J_r(x)$.

For each requested target, also form its composite-midpoint candidate with
$m=q$ panels, $h=\pi/m$, and nodes $\theta_j=(j+\tfrac12)h$,
$j=0,\ldots,m-1$, using $P_q$ as the interval for $\pi$. For $J_n$,
call the elementary-range algorithm for $\sin(\theta_j)$, form
$n\theta_j-x\sin(\theta_j)$, and call it for the cosine of that interval.
Let $Q_m$ be the interval sum $h\sum_j\cos(n\theta_j-x\sin\theta_j)$ and
$$E_J=\frac{h_{\max}^2}{24}\bigl((n+|x|)^2+|x|\bigr), \qquad h_{\max}=\sup(P_q)/m.$$
The candidate is $Q_m/P_q+[-E_J,E_J]$.
For the scaled $I$ target with $x>0$, call the elementary algorithm for
$\cos(\theta_j)$, form
$-x(1-\cos(\theta_j))$, call it for the real exponential, and also call it
for $\cos(n\theta_j)$. Let $Q_m$ be $h$ times the sum of the resulting
product intervals and set
$$E_I=\frac{h_{\max}^2}{24}\bigl((x+n)^2+x\bigr).$$
The candidate is $Q_m/P_q+[-E_I,E_I]$. The exact midpoint error lemmas
[[lem-bessel-integral-midpoint-error]] and
[[lem-scaled-modified-bessel-midpoint-error]] prove these inclusions.

For a $J_n(x)$ Miller candidate, only try this branch when $x>0$ and
$N=n+q\le N_{\max}$. Obtain $\operatorname{SeriesJ}(r)$ for
$r=0,1,n,N+1$; if any is unavailable, skip the branch. Set
$D_0=-J_1$, $D_1=J_0$, and compute
$D_{j+1}=2jD_j/x-D_{j-1}$ for $j=1,\ldots,N$ by interval arithmetic.
Set $u_{N+1}=0,u_N=1$, and compute
$u_{j-1}=2ju_j/x-u_{j+1}$ for $j=N,\ldots,1$. Require the intervals for
$D_{N+1}$, $u_s$, $J_s$, and $J_s+q_MD_s$ below to exclude zero. Form
$q_M=-J_{N+1}/D_{N+1}$. In the fixed order $s=0,1$, whenever the tests
pass, form
$$\widehat J_n=\frac{J_su_n}{u_s},\qquad E_M=\frac{q_M(J_sD_n-J_nD_s)}{J_s+q_MD_s}, \qquad C_M=\widehat J_n-E_M.$$
The exact finite terminal-contamination identity
[[lem-finite-miller-terminal-error-identity]] proves that each $C_M$
contains $J_n(x)$. The Casoratian lemma
[[lem-bessel-casoratian-invariant-positive]] supplies the independent
recurrence pair and positive invariant required by that identity.

Collect every available sound candidate for the requested target. If more
than one is available, intersect them; if the intersection is empty, discard
this stage. Round the selected candidate outward to precision $p$. Return
success at the first stage whose radius is at most $\varepsilon_a$. Set
relative_certified to true exactly when relative tolerance was requested,
zero is excluded, and the contract's relative-radius test passes; failure of
that relative test does not prevent absolute success. If no stage succeeds
before the finite caps, return inconclusive. No branch uses a limit in the
Miller terminal index.

items.title: Soundness of finite Airy enclosures

references.title: N. M. Temme, “Numerical aspects of special functions,” Acta Numerica 17 (2008), §2

items.statement:
Whenever [[alg-certified-airy-evaluation]] returns `success`, its interval or
rectangle contains the requested $\operatorname{Ai}(z)$ or
$\operatorname{Bi}(z)$ and passes the requested absolute-radius test. Any
relative certificate is valid only when the enclosure excludes zero. No
success guarantee is made for every input or finite cap. Every execution with finite
caps terminates.

items.title: Soundness of finite integer-order Bessel enclosures

references.title: DLMF, §10.2, Bessel functions of the first kind
N. M. Temme, “Numerical aspects of special functions,” Acta Numerica 17 (2008), §§2 and 4

items.statement:
Whenever [[alg-certified-integer-order-bessel-evaluation]] returns `success`,
its interval contains the requested $J_n(x)$ or scaled modified Bessel value
$e^{-x}I_n(x)$ and passes the requested absolute-radius test. A relative
certificate is valid only when zero is outside the interval and the relative
test passes. The theorem makes no success guarantee for every input or finite
cap. Every execution with finite caps terminates.

title: Stable special function recurrences and certified evaluation — Examples

items.title: The Gauss series disk and a continued logarithmic branch have different domains

references.title: N. M. Temme, “Numerical aspects of special functions,” Acta Numerica 17 (2008), §2

items.statement:
For $a=b=1$ and $c=2$, the Gauss-series branch in
[[def-fresnel-erf-and-hypergeometric-series]] is defined for $|z|<1$ and
there equals
$${}_2F_1(1,1;2;z)=\sum_{k=0}^\infty\frac{z^k}{k+1} =-\frac{\operatorname{Log}(1-z)}{z},$$
with value $1$ at $z=0$. The right side has a principal analytic
continuation to $\mathbb C\setminus[1,\infty)$, which includes $z=-2$; the
series evaluator correctly returns `domain` at $z=-2$ because this input lies
outside the defined power-series branch. This example distinguishes the
series branch's disk from the continuation branch's slit domain.

items.title: Subtracting erf from one amplifies absolute input errors in the tail

references.title: DLMF, §7.2, definitions of erf and erfc
N. M. Temme, “Numerical aspects of special functions,” Acta Numerica 17 (2008), §2

items.statement:
For $x>0$, suppose the inputs to the subtraction $1-\operatorname{erf}(x)$
are approximations $1+\delta_1$ and $\operatorname{erf}(x)+\delta_2$, where
$\delta_1,\delta_2$ are signed errors. Its output error is exactly
$\delta_1-\delta_2$, so its relative error is at most
$$\frac{|\delta_1|+|\delta_2|}{\operatorname{erfc}(x)}.$$
For fixed nonzero input error bounds, this conditioning factor grows without
bound as $x\to\infty$, because $\operatorname{erfc}(x)>0$ and tends to zero.
The identity $\operatorname{erfc}(x)=e^{-x^2}\operatorname{erfcx}(x)$ and a
certified direct $\operatorname{erfcx}$ enclosure avoid this particular
subtraction.

items.title: Least-term truncation of the erfcx asymptotic expansion

references.title: N. M. Temme, “Numerical aspects of special functions,” Acta Numerica 17 (2008), §§3 and 5

items.statement:
For $x\ge1$, let $N\ge1$ be an integer nearest to $x^2$, so
$N-\tfrac12\le x^2\le N+\tfrac12$. In the expansion from
[[lem-erfcx-asymptotic-remainder]], the magnitudes of the terms are
$$a_k(x)=\frac{(1/2)_k}{x^{2k+1}\sqrt\pi}.$$
The term $a_N(x)$ is minimal (ties are possible), and the signed remainder
after $N$ terms is bounded by exactly $a_N(x)$. For example, at $x=3$ the
least-term truncation is $N=9$. This describes optimal truncation by term
size; it does not assert convergence of the asymptotic series.

items.title: An arbitrarily small seed perturbation flips a later Bessel sign

references.title: N. M. Temme, “Numerical aspects of special functions,” Acta Numerica 17 (2008), §§2 and 4

items.statement:
At $x=1$, every $J_n(1)$ is positive and tends to zero as $n\to\infty$,
whereas the complementary recurrence solution $D_n(1)$ defined in
[[def-bessel-complementary-recurrence-solution]] is positive and unbounded
for $n\ge1$. Hence, for every $\varepsilon>0$, the perturbed seed pair
$$\widetilde J_0=J_0(1)-\varepsilon D_0(1),\qquad \widetilde J_1=J_1(1)-\varepsilon D_1(1)$$
can be arbitrarily close to the exact seeds, yet its forward recurrence
solution $\widetilde J_n=J_n(1)-\varepsilon D_n(1)$ is negative for some
index where the exact $J_n(1)$ is positive. This is a recurrence-sensitivity
example, not a claim that every floating-point implementation follows this
particular error direction.

items.title: Relative error becomes unavailable at an Airy zero

references.title: DLMF, §9.17(i), numerical evaluation of Airy functions
N. M. Temme, “Numerical aspects of special functions,” Acta Numerica 17 (2008), §2

items.statement:
There is a real $\xi<0$ with $\operatorname{Ai}(\xi)=0$. An absolute
enclosure remains meaningful there, but the relative certificate in
[[def-certified-evaluation-result-contract]] cannot be reported by an
enclosure containing zero. Near $\xi$, relative certification requires a
radius proportional to the small value $|\operatorname{Ai}(x)|$ and therefore
requires increasingly fine absolute enclosures.

items.title: Scaling keeps the modified Bessel value bounded as the unscaled value grows

references.title: DLMF, §10.40, asymptotic expansions for modified Bessel functions
N. M. Temme, “Numerical aspects of special functions,” Acta Numerica 17 (2008), §2

items.statement:
For $n=0$ and $x\ge0$, the scaled value $e^{-x}I_0(x)$ lies in $[0,1]$,
while $I_0(x)\to\infty$ as $x\to\infty$. Thus any fixed finite output
range for unscaled values is eventually exceeded, whereas the scaled value
remains bounded and can be evaluated directly from its scaled integral.
